analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The single patch hunk (head line ~1750) adds one table row listing DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS as environment variables forwarded into the launchd daemon, citing EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillChunkKey, stepTokenBudgetKey). The lines at that position were not supplied; only head lines 1-830 were provided, so I could not see the row in context. It is documentation-only: no code, authorization, attestation, encryption, or cache-storage control changes. I checked the supplied text against T-041 (prefix cache): it describes the encrypted SSD tier, default-on gating, HMAC lookup tags, the TTL and the SEC-035 accepted risk, none of which are altered. A newly forwarded tuning env var affects only prefill chunk size and step token budget, which are resource and performance parameters. It does not change the cache gate, TTL, name derivation or scope. The surrounding text is a reference to existing behavior and introduces no new trust-boundary claims. Open questions for integration: whether forwarding these two env vars into launchd (implemented outside this diff) lets a local operator influence only availability or performance, as expected for the ADV-001 operator, and whether any bound or validation exists on their values in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift. Neither was supplied, so the correct conclusion is that no regression is evidenced, not that the code is safe.
